examples.problem: Solve the inequality $x^2 \leq 2$ using the absolute value method.
examples.worked_solution:
Taking the square root of both sides of the inequality, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2} & \le 2 \\ \sqrt{{x}^{2}} & \le \sqrt{2} \\ |x| & \le \sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using the definition of absolute value, we must have

$$
-\sqrt 2\leq x \leq \sqrt 2.
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x \in [-\sqrt 2,\sqrt 2].$

feedback.problem: Solve the inequality  ${x}^{2}\ge 49$ using a graphical method.
feedback.worked_solution:
Bringing all the terms to the left-hand side, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2} & \ge 49 \\ {x}^{2}-49 & \ge 0.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we consider the corresponding parabola given by $\,y={x}^{2}-49\,$ and find its roots:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-49 & =0 \\ {x}^{2}-{7}^{2} & =0 \\ (x-7)(x+7) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

So the roots are $x=\pm 7.$ 

Solving the inequality ${x}^{2}-49\ge 0$ is equivalent to finding the values of $x$ for which the parabola $y={x}^{2}-49$ is above the $x$-axis or intersects the $x$-axis (where $y\ge 0$).

Since the leading coefficient of the quadratic expression is positive, the parabola opens upward. Therefore, the solution set lies outside the roots (including them), as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13965374/assets/5993bb434fca17beb9842d7963c5f560b4d8ef0bacadea4c120160d2ab93d131.png)

Therefore, the solution is $x\in (-\infty ,-7]\cup [7,\infty ).$
